optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Equipment Maintenance Services

professionalSummary.text: Senior analyst with two years of experience on a service‑platform team, specializing in gathering field‑service requirements, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, coordinating release scope, and documenting trainer hand‑over steps.
professionalSummary.witness: Spent about two years on the service-platform team as the analyst for the technician app: intake, stories, acceptance rounds and release write-ups.

experienceHighlights.text: Collected requirements from field technicians and depot staff through ride‑alongs and depot visits, producing user stories and acceptance criteria for offline checklist and parts‑scan features.
experienceHighlights.witness: Gathered requirements from field technicians and the depot team through ride‑alongs and depot visits, and wrote the user stories and acceptance criteria for the offline checklist and parts‑scan features of the technician app.

experienceHighlights.text: Organised acceptance rounds for four app releases, maintaining results per criterion in a shared sheet.
experienceHighlights.witness: Organised acceptance rounds for four app releases at the training site with a rotating group of technicians, and kept the results per criterion in a shared sheet.

experienceHighlights.text: Coordinated release scope with engineering lead and field‑service manager, documenting decision ownership.
experienceHighlights.witness: Coordinated release scope with the engineering lead and the field‑service manager in the release planning meeting; the engineering lead decided scope and dates, and the field‑service manager approved the rollout order across regions.

experienceHighlights.text: Authored release hand‑over documentation for regional trainers, noting device compatibility and trainer steps.
experienceHighlights.witness: Wrote up each app release for the regional trainers, flagging that parts‑scan only worked on the newer handheld model and listing the steps trainers had to take over.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Parts‑scan story set with acceptance criteria and acceptance‑round results sheet, traceable via ticket numbers.
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the parts‑scan story set with acceptance criteria and the results sheet from one acceptance round; ticket numbers are included so entries can be traced.

skills.text: Requirements gathering, user story writing, acceptance criteria definition, acceptance testing coordination, release scope management, trainer hand‑over documentation.

optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume and work sample establish the candidate’s experience in gathering requirements, writing user stories and acceptance criteria, organising acceptance rounds, coordinating release scope, and documenting trainer hand‑over steps. They do not provide evidence that delivered features shortened average on‑site visit times.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate meets all role requirements except for evidence of visit‑time reduction.

role.roleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Equipment Maintenance Services

evidence.text: Gathered requirements from field technicians and the depot team through ride‑alongs and depot visits, and wrote the user stories and acceptance criteria for the offline checklist and parts‑scan features of the technician app.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of requirement gathering and story creation.

evidence.text: Work sample: the parts‑scan story set with acceptance criteria and the results sheet from one acceptance round; ticket numbers are included so entries can be traced.
evidence.notes: Concrete artifact demonstrating stories and criteria.

evidence.text: Organised acceptance rounds for four app releases at the training site with a rotating group of technicians, and kept the results per criterion in a shared sheet.
evidence.notes: Explicit description of acceptance rounds and record keeping.

evidence.text: Hiring manager pre‑read: a slide from the candidate's portfolio deck says 'average visit time down 22 minutes after parts‑scan'; the slide has no source, period or region, and the candidate said in the screen that the number came from a regional manager's email he no longer has.
evidence.notes: Unverified claim with no supporting data.

missingEvidence: Verified baseline visit time data, post‑implementation visit time data, statistical analysis showing reduction, region and period context

evidence.text: Coordinated release scope with the engineering lead and the field‑service manager in the release planning meeting; the engineering lead decided scope and dates, and the field‑service manager approved the rollout order across regions.
evidence.notes: Clear statement of scope coordination and decision ownership.

evidence.text: Wrote up each app release for the regional trainers, flagging that parts‑scan only worked on the newer handheld model and listing the steps trainers had to take over.
evidence.notes: Documented trainer hand‑over steps and limitations.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has experience gathering field‑service requirements and writing user stories with acceptance criteria.
supportedClaims.witness: Gathered requirements from field technicians and the depot team through ride‑alongs and depot visits, and wrote the user stories and acceptance criteria for the offline checklist and parts‑scan features of the technician app.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has organized acceptance rounds and maintained results.
supportedClaims.witness: Organised acceptance rounds for four app releases at the training site with a rotating group of technicians, and kept the results per criterion in a shared sheet.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has coordinated release scope with engineering and field‑service manager, documenting decision ownership.
supportedClaims.witness: Coordinated release scope with the engineering lead and the field‑service manager in the release planning meeting; the engineering lead decided scope and dates, and the field‑service manager approved the rollout order across regions.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate has written trainer hand‑over documentation with limitations.
supportedClaims.witness: Wrote up each app release for the regional trainers, flagging that parts‑scan only worked on the newer handheld model and listing the steps trainers had to take over.

unsupportedClaims.claim: Delivered features shortened average on‑site visit times by 22 minutes.
unsupportedClaims.reason: No verifiable data or analysis provided; claim originates from an unreferenced slide and an email no longer available.
unsupportedClaims.requiredFollowUp: Provide baseline visit time data, post‑implementation visit time data, statistical analysis, and source documentation.

missingEvidenceGaps.gap: Verified baseline and post‑implementation visit time metrics, statistical significance, region and period context.

interviewSignalRisks.text: Unverified claim of 22‑minute reduction in visit time.
interviewSignalRisks.recommendedHandling: Ask for source data, request statistical analysis, and verify with independent metrics.

followUpQuestions.question: Can you provide the baseline average on‑site visit time, the post‑implementation average, and the statistical analysis that demonstrates the 22‑minute reduction?
followUpQuestions.evidenceTarget: Baseline and post‑implementation visit time data, statistical analysis, source documentation.

Evidence for the key performance metric of reduced on‑site visit time is missing and currently unverified. Human review is required to decide whether to proceed based on the absence of this evidence.
